question: Two lines are perpendicular if their slopes multiply to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any two non-vertical perpendicular lines, their slopes are negative reciprocals.

Shortcut: m₁ × m₂ = −1

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two lines are perpendicular to each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e84678bf61d235fdd7823e45e834eb872a4f74184003d7d52ba3edd917e7eff9.png] 

⇒ Let the slope of the first line be m₁.

⇒ Let the slope of the second line be m₂.

⇒ If Line 1 is perpendicular to Line 2, then m₂ = −1 / m₁.

⇒ Multiplying both sides by m₁:

⇒ m₁ × m₂ = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Parallel Lines Condition

Two lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal, i.e., m₁ = m₂.

Slope Formula

The slope m of a line passing through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by m = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).

Angle Between Two Lines

The tangent of the angle θ between two lines is tan θ = |(m₂ − m₁) ÷ (1 + m₁ × m₂)|.</p
